svg.metadata: {"device_model":{"id":"elab.hobbyist-devices.v1","pwm":"Generic powered PWM clock: configurable 10..1000 Hz and 10..90 percent duty. Rise/fall each occupy 5 percent of a period. Duty includes the rising phase. Output uses complementary 50 ohm paths, 1 Gohm off bleed, 1 Mohm supply load and smooth supply enable from 2 to 3 V. No feedback compensation, current limit, temporal dead time, switching loss, noise or hardware rating. Buck examples simulate external switched power stages, not an averaged converter.","opamp_dynamics":"Optional dominant-pole and slew-limited compensation for the unchanged generic op-amp output stage. Gain-bandwidth and slew rate are saved settings; a private 1 nF compensation capacitor charges from the modeled rails, preserving KCL, energy and explicit dissipation. The output target remains bounded by the present rails even when stored compensation voltage outlasts a falling supply. Existing op-amps without dynamics retain their original equations. No fitted silicon identity, noise, offset, multiple poles, protection or thermal ratings.","shift_register":"Generic 8-bit serial-in parallel-out register with separate positive-edge shift and output-latch clocks, active-low shift clear, active-low parallel output enable, and serial cascade output independent of output enable. State starts cleared; power loss clears both registers. Sixteen internal D memories reuse sequential-v1 edge/guard laws; internal data uses ideal logic rails with explicit 1 Gohm loading, while finite 50 ohm drive is applied only at public Q/SERIAL outputs. A logic-v1 inverter maps active-low clear. Simultaneous shift/latch/cascade clocks sample pre-edge data. Parallel buffers use 50 ohm paths when enabled and 1 Gohm to their selected rail when disabled; OE interpolates across the declared 30/70 percent input interval. Serial has its own 50 ohm buffer. No package pinout, propagation or setup/hold timing, metastability, current/thermal ratings.","sound":"Generic capacitive piezo sounder and DC-powered active buzzer. Passive piezo uses explicit capacitance and leakage; acoustic preview is a normalized illustrative terminal-voltage signal, not calibrated SPL or a mechanical/room simulation. Active buzzer uses a passive voltage-dependent DC load and an ideal acoustic oscillator; no electrical oscillator ripple. Opening or simulating a project never plays audio. Preview rendering, playback, stopping and WAV export are explicit shared commands."},"diode_model":{"id":"elab.generic-silicon-diode.v1","is_a":1e-9,"n":1.7,"rs_ohm":1,"temperature_c":27,"limitations":"Generic silicon junction with Shockley forward/reverse leakage and single H-bridge with IN1/IN2 and active-high ENABLE/PWM. Enabled 10 drives forward, 01 reverse, 00 brakes to GND and 11 brakes to VM; ENABLE low coasts. Inputs are local to GND: \u003c=0.8 V low, \u003e=2 V high. Intermediate levels use a smooth nonoverlapping conductance transition, not a valid digital state. Each active leg is 0.25 ohm with a 1 Gohm off path; four passive piecewise-linear clamp diodes remain active during coast and power-off (0.65 V knee plus 0.25 ohm). Input pulldowns are 1 Mohm; supply load is 100 kohm. Supply enable rises smoothly from 2 to 3 V; \u003c=2 V disables active legs. Bidirectional leg conduction and diode paths allow regenerative current into VM. No temporal dead time, propagation delay, gate charge, current limiting, thermal protection, switching loss, physical ratings or fitted manufacturer identity. Connect all controls and both supply pins; the supply must accommodate returned energy.
